transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, doctor, I... I hope it's okay that I'm here. I don't want to be a bother, but things have just been a little... overwhelming lately. I came in because, well, I've been having some trouble with my in-laws. We've been arguing, which is normal, I suppose, but... it's more than that. I just know they're using the church altar and the parish committee to sort of... push me out. They want everyone to forget everything I've done for this family. Does that make sense? I just... I don't want to sound like I'm complaining too much, I just need a little help sorting it out, if that's alright.
Have you ever experienced any unusual thoughts or beliefs that others might find strange, such as feeling like you're being targeted, followed, or that people are plotting against you?

Well... I suppose that's sort of what I was trying to explain just a moment ago. I know it probably sounds terrible of me to say, and I really do try to see the good in everyone, I promise. But... yes, I suppose I do feel targeted. 

Like I mentioned, it’s not just normal family bickering with my in-laws. I just know, in my heart, that they are using the church altar and the parish committee to deliberately push me out. It feels like they've coordinated it all to make everyone completely forget everything I’ve done for this family over the years. 

I know that must sound so strange to hear... does that sound completely awful of me to think that? I just hope you don't think I'm being overly dramatic...
Do you ever question or doubt this belief about your in-laws trying to push you out through the church, or does it feel absolutely certain to you?

Oh, I... I really wish I could say it was just my imagination. I know it would be so much easier for everyone, and for you, if I was just... misunderstanding things. I try so hard to be a good, forgiving person, I really do. 

But... no, I don't really doubt it. I hope that doesn't make me sound stubborn or mean-spirited. It's just... like I was saying, I just know they aren't merely arguing with me over normal family things. I can see exactly how they're using the altar and the parish committee to push me out. It's just too coordinated to be an accident. They really are trying to make everyone completely forget everything I've done for this family all these years. 

I've tried to talk myself out of it, I really have, because I want to think the best of them. But the feeling is just... it's certain. Is it terrible of me to be so sure about something like that? I just want to be a good person... I hope you can understand where I'm coming from.
Has there ever been a time when you didn’t believe that your in-laws were trying to push you out through the church, or has this feeling always been present and certain?

Well, no, it hasn't always been like this. I... I really used to get along with them, or at least I tried my absolute best to. I always wanted us to be a close family. 

It really only started recently... I'd say this whole... crisis, if you want to call it that, has been going on for about two months now. It all started after we had a bit of a disagreement over the Día de los Muertos altar. I just wanted to honor our loved ones the right way, you know? But ever since that fight, things have just felt so different. 

I really hope I don't sound like I'm holding a grudge. I know two months might seem like a long time to be upset about something like that, but that's when I really started to notice what they were doing with the parish committee. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right so you don't think I'm just being difficult.
Can you think of any specific evidence or events that support your belief that your in-laws are coordinating through the church to push you out?

Oh, um... well, I know I keep bringing up the same things, and I really hope I'm not testing your patience by repeating myself... I just want to make sure I'm answering you properly. 

As far as, you know, hard evidence... it's... it's hard to explain without sounding petty, and I really try so hard not to be a petty person. But it's just in how they act. Like I mentioned before, I came in to get help because I finally realized they weren't just arguing with me over little everyday things. I could just see exactly how they were using their roles on the parish committee, and the way they took over the altar... they make sure I'm excluded from all the important decisions now. 

It's all just so they can push me out and make the whole community completely forget what I’ve done for our family all these years. I don't have, like, a piece of paper or a recording to prove it to you, but I just know it's happening. 

I'm sorry, I know that's probably not exactly the kind of concrete proof you were asking for... am I being helpful at all? I just really don't want you to think I'm making things up to be spiteful.
Even when others may not see the same things you do, does it still feel completely real and true to you, no matter what anyone else says or how much they try to reassure you?

Oh, I... I know people try to tell me I'm just overthinking it, and I always try to smile and agree with them because I really hate causing any friction. I want to be agreeable, I truly do. When people try to reassure me, I listen, and I thank them, because I know they mean well. 

But... yes, inside, it still feels completely real to me. I'm so sorry, I know I must sound like a broken record saying this again, and I really hope you aren't getting frustrated with me. But like I said when I first came in... I just knew my in-laws were not just arguing with me over a simple disagreement. No matter how much anyone tries to calm me down, I can see that they are using the altar and the parish committee to push me out. It just feels so true that they want to make everyone forget what I have done for this family. 

I wish I could just accept the reassurance and let it go, I really do. It would make me a much better wife and mother-in-law if I could just brush it off. Does it make me a terrible person that I can't just let go of it, even when people tell me it isn't true? I promise I'm trying my best to work through this with you.

Even when people show you that there’s no real proof or when they give you other explanations, does it still feel completely true to you that your in-laws are trying to push you out through the church?

I know... I know it probably sounds like I'm just being stubborn. And I really, really don't want to be a difficult patient. I try to listen to what people say, and I nod and agree because I don't want to cause a fuss. I know they're just trying to help when they give me other explanations. 

But... yes. It still feels completely true. I... I know I keep saying this, and I'm so sorry for repeating myself, but it's the whole reason I came in to get help. I just knew, deep down, that my in-laws were not just arguing with me over a silly little disagreement. I could see that they were using the altar and the parish committee to push me out. They want everyone to forget everything I've done for this family over the years. 

I know you might think I'm just being overly sensitive, and maybe I am a little bit... but I just can't shake the feeling that it's all true, even when there's no proof. Is that... is that okay to admit? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers so we can figure this out.

Even when people give you logical explanations or show you that your concerns might not make sense, does it still feel completely true to you that your in-laws are trying to push you out through the church?

I... I really hope you aren't getting frustrated with me for saying the same thing again. I know I must seem so unreasonable when you put it like that... when you say logical explanations. I always try to see reason, I really do. I don't want you to think I'm the kind of person who just ignores logic or refuses to listen to others. 

But... yes, doctor, it still feels true. I mean, that's exactly why I finally came in to see you. I just... I knew they weren't just arguing with me over nothing. I could see it all happening... the way they were using the parish committee and taking over the altar. It's all just to push me out and erase everything I've built for this family. 

I know it doesn't make sense to other people, and I'm so sorry if it sounds crazy to you. I really am trying to look at it logically like you said... but I just can't make the feeling go away. Am I being too difficult by saying that? I just want to be honest with you so I can get better.

I know my in-laws aren't just having a normal family argument with me. I can see it so clearly, how they're using the parish committee and the altar to just... push me completely out of the picture.
